title: The ten essentials
summary: Pack these on every trip into the backcountry, even a short one.

blocks.p: Pack these on every trip into the backcountry, even a short one.

blocks.cap: The ten essential systems, as The Mountaineers list them.

list: Navigation: map and compass, plus a phone with a GPS app or a GPS unit, and a spare battery.
Sun protection: sunglasses, sunscreen and a hat.
Fire: waterproof matches or a lighter, and fire starter.
Emergency shelter: space blanket, bivy sack or tarp.
Extra food: a day’s worth beyond your plan.
Extra water, and a way to treat more.
Extra layers: insulation and rain gear.

blocks.p: This list follows The Mountaineers’ Ten Essential Systems. The NYS DEC list for New York hikers also adds a whistle, a signal mirror and insect protection.
Tell someone where you’re going and when you’ll be back. Carry a whistle: it carries farther than your voice and takes less effort, and three blasts is a distress signal.

sources.name: The Mountaineers, Ten Essentials: The Classic List and the Ten Essential Systems (citing Mountaineering: The Freedom of the Hills, 9th edition), Olympia Branch handout
sources.used: The ten systems this list follows: navigation (map, compass, GPS device or phone with GPS app, extra batteries or battery pack), headlamp plus extra batteries, sun protection (sunglasses, sunscreen), first aid, knife, fire (matches, lighter and tinder), shelter carried at all times, extra food, extra water or the means to purify, extra clothes

sources.name: National Park Service, Ten Essentials
sources.used: Paper map and compass or GPS, extra battery for your phone; sunglasses, sunscreen and hats; extra clothing such as a rain shell and jacket; headlamp and extra batteries; first-aid kit; waterproof matches or lighter and fire starters; knife or multi-tool; an extra day's supply of food; water and knowing where to find water you can treat; tent, tarp, bivy sack or emergency space blanket; tell someone where you're going and when to expect you back
